skills.name: orchestration-wayfinder
limitations: Codex and Claude Code runtime addenda require matching task, deadline, and GitHub tracker facilities. No Cursor addendum exists. The workflow has explicit merge authority when invoked; installation does not invoke it.
localPatches: 2026-10-01: Added T3.md and pointers to it from SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, and CODEX.md. Inside T3 Code, grilling and prototype tickets get their own T3 thread in the sidebar, cast natively (UI prototypes on claude-fable-5-1), watched by one t3-kickoff waiter per thread, and archived after the ticket closes. Reason: Michael works HITL tickets by switching threads in T3 Code while the conductor keeps the frontier moving.

2026-10-02: Implementation tickets now ship as a draft pull request that the qa-swarm skill hands off as ready for review, instead of a merged commit; the map's Notes can grant merge authority. A dependent implementation ticket stacks on its blocker's pull request branch. qa-swarm replaces the single adversarial reviewer, and its Fable 5.1 and GPT-6.1 Sol lanes are exempt from the retired-cast rule. Reason: Michael wants near-full autonomy, reviews every pull request himself before it merges.

2026-10-03: Removed the Opus worker default, Anthropic-only casting, strongest-model fallback, and Fable UI prototype choice. Worker models and reasoning now use runtime defaults unless the user requests an override; T3 threads explicitly carry the conductor's provider and model to avoid CLI fallback choices. Reason: Michael wants Wayfinder to respect session model choices without forcing expensive models or limiting research fan-out.

2026-10-03: Restored Fable 5.1 as the sole fixed worker model for all UI work, including prototypes, implementation, and nested UI workers. T3 UI threads select the provider offering claude-fable-5-1; other work keeps runtime defaults. Unavailable Fable dispatch records a blocker instead of substituting another model. Reason: Michael wants Fable 5.1 fixed for UI work without restoring expensive defaults elsewhere or limiting research fan-out.
2026-10-03: Route Claude model selection through home/.agents/AGENTS.md instead of fixed Fable defaults. Reason: Michael chooses models explicitly or by task complexity.

2026-10-05: In T3.md, an architecture prototype parks with its first round of open decision cards as the pending question, and each round of answers is feedback. Reason: the architecture brief is shaped in decision rounds, not one question.

2026-10-05: Implementation tickets ship as a reviewed draft pull request: one review from the other model family, or qa-swarm where AGENTS.md calls for it. A park stays parked until the human answers, and the conductor never re-dispatches a worker to keep reviewing. Follow-up work goes to the ticket's existing worker. Reason: qa-swarm on every ticket, and workers re-dispatched past its round cap, spent most of a week's Claude and GPT quota in a day.

portablePatches: Personal agent instructions replaced with recipient-neutral rules. Git identity, hub authorization, providers, proxy, machine inventory, and pruning are excluded.
Single-Claude pilot uses an independent read-only Claude review when a second provider is unavailable; production repositories retain their own review requirements.
QA panel uses available Claude workers. Skill prose refers to the recipient, writing-voice uses a neutral guide, and remote handoff uses their SSH aliases. Fixtures retain example repository names.
